metadata.case_name: CHAN HANG YING VANESSA v. LO KA WAI

plaintiff.occupation_before: Administrative clerk / human resources assistant; part-time ballet teacher/dancer
plaintiff.occupation_after: Ballet teacher; proprietor of Nessa Dance Studio (owner/operator)
plaintiff.education_level: Educated up to Form 7; Advanced II level from the Royal Academy of Dance (2007); certificate in human resources management

injuries.description: minor head injury and post-concussion syndrome
source: The plaintiff was diagnosed to suffer minor head injury and post-concussion syndrome.

injuries.description: neck sprain injury / soft tissue injury of neck
source: The diagnosis was neck sprain injury.
The experts agreed that the plaintiff suffered soft tissue injury of neck and left shoulder.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine, unspecified

injuries.description: left supraspinatus tendinosis (strain of supraspinatus tendon; tendinitis/tendinosis of supraspinatus and subscapularis)
source: MRI of the plaintiffs left shoulder was performed on 15 November 2010 which showed that the plaintiff suffered left supraspinatus tendinosis.
Dr Chiens diagnosis was soft tissue sprain of the neck and strained left shoulder supraspinatus tendon.

Further MRI of the plaintiffs left shoulder was performed on 17 June 2013. ... supraspinatus and subscapularis showed some minor signal changes consistent with tendinosis/tendinitis with no definite full thickness tear and no evidence of partial thickness tear over 50%.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle or tendon of the rotator cuff of shoulder

injuries.description: small haematoma with surrounding muscular oedema in the mid part of the deltoid muscle (post-injury change)
source: small haematoma with surrounding muscular oedema in the mid part of the deltoid muscle, consistent with small haematoma and oedema post injury.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at shoulder or upper arm level

injuries.description: fibrotic deltoid muscles with mild inflammation and congestion over the articular side of the cuff (intraoperative findings)
source: Intraoperative findings found fibrotic deltoid muscles with cracking wound on establishing surgical portals and mild signs of inflammation at the lateral rim of acromial.
There were features of congestion over the articular side of the cuff.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of multiple muscles or tendons at shoulder or upper arm level

manifestations.description: reduced range of motion of neck (flexion 1/2 and extension 1/3 of normal at one point; later clinical limited neck flexion and poor extension)
reduced range of motion of left shoulder (narrower than right in flexion, abduction and internal rotation; painful arc)
weakness of supraspinatus and subscapularis muscle power
wasting of infraspinatus and supraspinatus muscles of the left shoulder
positive impingement sign on the left side
reduced sensation (decreased 10% to 20% over left lateral arm and left lateral forearm)
scar hypertrophy particularly over the lateral aspect of the shoulder; residual congestion and dark pigmentation
intermittent/on-and-off pain requiring occasional treatment and causing difficulty sleeping
limited ability in lifting objects by left hand / reduced functional use of left hand

treatments_received: Ambulance to Prince of Wales Hospital (A&E) with oxygen
In-patient admission at Prince of Wales Hospital for 3 days
Physiotherapy at Prince of Wales Hospital
Physiotherapy at Yan Chai Hospital (multiple sessions)
Neurosurgery follow-up at Prince of Wales Hospital (2010-2011)
MRI of left shoulder (15 Nov 2010; 10 Nov 2011; 17 June 2013)
Private consultations and treatment by Dr Eric Chien (Centre for Orthopaedic Surgery) since 16 June 2011
Arthroscopic decompression of the subacromial space (operation performed on 2013-12-18 by Dr Chien)
Post-operative private physiotherapy and clinic follow-up at the Centre
About 10 sessions of acupuncture therapy from Chinese medicine practitioners
treatments_future: ongoing physiotherapy (post-trial) and regular follow-up treatment by Dr Chien
serial steroid injection to scar (suggested as an option by Dr Chien but not accepted as necessary by the party experts)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Injuries made it difficult, if not impossible, for the plaintiff's left arm to perform overhead movements, affecting her ability to perform certain postures for ballet dancing and reducing opportunities to participate in performances and concerts.
Scar hypertrophy particularly over the lateral aspect of the shoulder with residual congestion and dark pigmentation after surgery.
Reduced range of motion of the neck and left shoulder and difficulty in overhead activities.
